title: "Always online: serve stale cache when the origin cannot provide a fresh response"
sidebarTitle: Serve stale cache from CDN
description: Configure Always Online via the Customer Portal, REST API, or Terraform to serve stale cache when the origin cannot provide a fresh response.
---

import { MethodSwitch, MethodSection } from "/snippets/method-switch.jsx";

<MethodSwitch>
  <MethodSection id="portal" label="Customer Portal">

<p>The Always Online option serves stale cached content when the origin cannot provide a usable fresh response, and those responses include the `X-Cache: Stale` header. When none of the selected stale conditions applies, the CDN resumes serving fresh responses.</p>

<p>The option serves stale content for these conditions:</p>

| Condition | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Error | Network or connectivity failure |
| Updating | Cached object is being refreshed |
| Timeout | Origin response timed out |
| Invalid Header | Origin returned an invalid header |
| 403, 404, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 | Origin returned that HTTP status |

<p>The CDN can serve only objects that are already present in cache. If some page assets are not already cached when a stale condition occurs, those images, stylesheets, or other files can still fail to load.</p>

## Always online

<p>Turn it on for the conditions that should serve stale content.</p>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the CDN resource">
    In the [Gcore Customer Portal](https://portal.gcore.com), navigate to **CDN** and click the CDN resource.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open Always online">
    In the sidebar, click **Cache**. In the expanded menu, click **Always online**.

    <Frame>![Resource settings with Cache expanded in the sidebar and Always online selected, showing the Enable always online toggle](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/always-online-provide-the-stale-cache-if-the-origin-is-unavailable/always-online-provide-the-stale-cache-if-the-origin-is-unavailable-image1.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enable Always online">
    Enable the **Enable always online** toggle.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select stale conditions">
    In the **Serve stale cached content in case of the following errors** field, select the conditions.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save the resource">
    Click **Save changes**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="api" label="REST API">

<p>When `stale` is enabled for a selected condition, the CDN serves the cached response and marks it with `X-Cache: Stale`. When none of the selected stale conditions applies, the CDN resumes serving fresh responses.</p>

<p>The CDN can serve only objects that are already present in cache. If some page assets are not already cached when a stale condition occurs, those images, stylesheets, or other files can still fail to load.</p>

<Info>
An [API&nbsp;token](/account-settings/api-tokens) is required.
</Info>

<p>Export these variables. `CDN_RESOURCE_ID` is the `id` from [list&nbsp;CDN&nbsp;resources](/api-reference/cdn/cdn-resources/list-cdn-resources).</p>

```bash
export GCORE_API_KEY="{YOUR_API_KEY}"
export CDN_RESOURCE_ID="{YOUR_RESOURCE_ID}"
```

## Stale values

<p>`value` accepts `error`, `updating`, `timeout`, `invalid_header`, `http_403`, `http_404`, `http_429`, `http_500`, `http_502`, `http_503`, and `http_504`. `error` is a network or connectivity failure, and `updating` is a cache refresh.</p>

<p>Both `enabled` and `value` are required. When `enabled` is true, `value` must contain at least one condition; an empty list returns HTTP 400.</p>

<p>The request below enables stale delivery for `http_404` and `http_500`.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os
    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "stale": {"enabled": True, "value": ["http_404", "http_500"]},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.stale.enabled, resource.options.stale.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        resource, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                Stale: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsStale{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   []string{"http_404", "http_500"},
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        fmt.Println(resource.Options.Stale.Enabled, resource.Options.Stale.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "stale": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": ["http_404", "http_500"]
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "options": {
        "stale": {
          "enabled": true,
          "value": ["http_404", "http_500"]
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="terraform" label="Terraform">

<p>Set `stale` so the CDN serves a cached response when the origin cannot provide a usable fresh response, using the [Terraform&nbsp;provider](/developer-tools/terraform/overview) v2. The served response includes `X-Cache: Stale`. When none of the selected stale conditions applies, the CDN resumes serving fresh responses. The CDN can serve only objects that are already present in cache.</p>

<p>`value` accepts `error` (network or connectivity failure), `updating` (cache refresh), `timeout` (origin response timed out), `invalid_header` (origin returned an invalid header), `http_403`, `http_404`, `http_429`, `http_500`, `http_502`, `http_503`, and `http_504`. `enabled` and `value` are both required. When `enabled` is true, an empty `value` list returns HTTP 400. Leaving `stale` out of `options` leaves the stored option unchanged. Run `terraform apply` after editing `options`.</p>

## Serve stale content

<p>Set `enabled` to true. With `http_404` and `http_500`, a 404 or 500 from the origin is served from cache and marked with `X-Cache: Stale`.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    stale = {
      enabled = true
      value   = ["http_404", "http_500"]
    }
  }
}
```

</MethodSection>
